answer: Running 277 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the opal schedule in the sable ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ripple checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 35 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
